html:
In April 1900 the chiefs of Tutuila signed a deed ceding their island to the United States; the chiefs of Manuʻa followed in 1904. Together these islands became American Samoa.

The US Navy ran the territory from its station at Pago Pago, one of the best harbours in the South Pacific, until 1951. The deed promised to respect Samoan land and custom, and most land is still held by families under their chiefs.

People born in American Samoa are US nationals but not citizens, unlike in Guam. The split from German Samoa under the Tripartite Convention is the reason for it.
